_: What each routed repository's merge path requires. Every check here can refuse a
merge, and nothing on this host runs any of them.
This file was a coverage claim until onevcs 0.11.0 removed the gate concept. It
recorded, per identity, which required checks `config/onevcs.rules.yml`'s gate
reproduced and which it did not — and the first category is now empty by
construction, because no rule names a verifier and this host front-runs nothing.
So it is an inventory instead, and that is what makes the audit meaningful: the
question `just repos --audit-gate-coverage` answers is no longer "is our gate the
whole bar" but "what can refuse this merge", which is the only question left.
The reason beside each check says what that check *is*, out of a small closed
vocabulary. That is real information rather than a leftover: an operator reading
nine required checks wants to know which one is the verdict on their tree
(`tree-verdict`) and which are cross-OS lanes, packaging, or a pull-request
policy they cannot affect from a branch. Nothing is claimed by omission — a
required check this file does not carry is a declaration error, and the audit
treats an identity it does not know at all as uncovered rather than as clean.
`tests/e2e/test_repo_registry_apply_e2e.py` asks GitHub what each branch really
requires and fails when this file disagrees, so a check added, renamed, or newly
required after this was written is found here rather than by a blocked change
request. That is why the tier is uncached: its input is other repositories'
branch protection, which no `nx.json` key covers.
Add an identity together with its rule: `just repos-apply` refuses a checkout no
rule names, and the suite refuses a rule this file does not classify.

reasons.tree-verdict: runs the repository's own verification of the working tree on the merge path's runner: the verdict on the change itself
reasons.other-os: runs on an operating system this host does not have
reasons.pull-request: judges the pull request itself (its title, or its commits) rather than the tree, and does not exist until the branch is pushed
reasons.published-artifact: installs, packages, or publishes a release artifact rather than judging the working tree
reasons.visual-baseline: captures screenshots in CI's pinned container and classifies them against a hosted baseline
reasons.paid-turn: spends a real agent turn against a paid provider
reasons.network-advisory: resolves a network-fetched advisory database whose contents change independently of the branch
reasons.ci-selection: a CI job that only selects which lanes run and carries no verdict about the tree
reasons.judged-remotely: runs on the merge path's own runner and carries a verdict nothing outside CI reproduces

github.com/nickderobertis/ai-orchestrato.note: The one local-direct identity: it opens no change request, so its merge path declares no required checks at all. What verifies it is its own executable `pre-push` hook, which `onevcs` reaches through the lender's `core.hooksPath` in the clone a publication works in.

github.com/nickderobertis/llmlint.note: Runs an llmlint job on every pull request but has never required it, so it is not a check that can refuse the merge and is not inventoried here.

github.com/nickderobertis/onetaskgraph.note: Registered before the repository has any CI: its `main` declares no required checks yet, so nothing can refuse a merge to it, and this inventory is empty because that is the truth rather than because it is unrecorded. The build's foundation change makes six checks required, and the node that lands it corrects this entry in the same run.

github.com/nickderobertis/screencomp.note: Runs an llmlint job on every pull request but has never required it, so it is not a check that can refuse the merge and is not inventoried here.
